=== Morphological Assessment Form ===
A. Leaf Arrangement & Architecture
    1. Leaf relative position (alternate / opposite / whorled): alternate (leaves are attached at different nodes along the stem, alternating sides, visible across multiple images)
    2. Leaf spacing (clustered / distal): distal (leaves are spaced apart along the stem rather than tightly clustered at the tips)
B. Leaf Complexity
    3. Leaf complexity (simple / compound): simple (each leaf blade is undivided and attached directly to the stem via a petiole)
    4. Compound leaf type, ONLY if leaf complexity is compound (odd-pinnate / even-pinnate): N/A
    5. Number of leaflets (integer estimate 2, 4, 8, …): N/A
    6. Leaflet arrangement (opposite / alternate / subopposite): N/A
C. Leaf Morphology
    7. Leaf margin (entire / toothed) AND if toothed (dentate, serrate, etc.)): entire (leaf edges appear smooth without teeth or serrations in all views)
    8. Leaf shape (elliptic, obovate, lanceolate, etc.): lanceolate (leaves are elongated and tapering towards both the base and apex)
    9. Leaf apex (acute, obtuse, acuminate): acuminate (the apex tapers to a distinct, elongated point, clearly visible in close-up)
    10. Leaf base (rounded, cordate, cuneate): cuneate (the leaf base tapers down to the petiole, appearing wedge-shaped)
    11. Venation type (pinnate / palmate / parallel): pinnate (a central midrib is visible with lateral veins branching off it)
    12. Secondary veins (visibility, spacing, number): visible and distinct (veins are clearly visible against the green leaf surface, spacing appears regular)
    13. Leaf surface features (glabrous, shiny, dull, rugose): shiny (the leaf surface reflects light, indicating a smooth and somewhat glossy texture)
    14. Leaf surface trichomes (present / absent): absent (no visible hairs on the leaf surface in the close-up images)
    15. Petiole length (short / long): short (the petiole connecting the leaf blade to the stem is relatively short compared to the leaf length)
    16. Petiole features (winged / grooved / terete): terete (the petioles appear cylindrical and round in cross-section)
D. Stem & Shoot Traits
    17. Stem type, may not be visible (woody / herbaceous): woody (the stem appears thin, rigid, and brown, characteristic of a woody seedling)
    18. Stem trichomes (present / absent): absent (the stem appears smooth without visible hairs)
    19. Stem color: brown (the visible parts of the stem are a dark brown color)
    20. Stem texture (smooth / ridged / lenticellate): smooth (the stem surface appears relatively smooth without obvious ridges or lenticels)
E. Other Visible Seedling Traits
    21. Stipules, sometimes visible only in close-up images (present / absent): absent (no stipules are visible at the base of the petioles in the provided images)
    22. Latex, rarely visible but extremely diagnostic when present (present / not observed): not observed (no latex is visible)
    23. Pulvinus, for Fabaceae family only (present / absent): absent (no pulvinus is visible at the base of the petioles)
    24. Tendrils (present / absent): absent (no tendrils are present on the seedling)
F. Notes: The seedling is marked with a pink tag. Some leaves show minor damage (small holes and missing margin sections).
